name: InfiniAI Pulse — weekly AI & Data newsletter

parameters.jsCode:
// Turn the collected articles into one prompt for Gemini.
const a = $json.articles;

const today  = new Date();
const monday = new Date(today); monday.setDate(today.getDate() - 6);
const fmt = d => d.toLocaleDateString('en-GB', { day: 'numeric', month: 'long', year: 'numeric' });
const weekLabel = `${fmt(monday)} - ${fmt(today)}`;

// Issue number = weeks since the first issue. Change the anchor date to yours.
const anchor = new Date('2026-01-07T00:00:00Z');
const issueNo = String(Math.floor((today - anchor) / (7 * 864e5)) + 1);

const feedText = a.map((x, i) =>
  `[${i + 1}]${x.image ? ' [HAS-IMAGE]' : ''} ${x.date} | ${x.source}\n${x.title}\n${x.summary}\n${x.link}`
).join('\n\n');

const prompt = `You are the art director AND editor of "InfiniAI Pulse", a weekly AI & Data
newsletter published by the AI & Data Office at SLT-MOBITEL, a Sri Lankan telecom group.

The issue is a POSTER, not an article. Readers scan it in two minutes. Every idea must earn
its place as a visual tile: a picture, a number, a matrix, a ranked list, a comparison, a chart
or a short quote. Prose is the last resort, never the default.

Below are raw news items for the week of ${weekLabel}. Items marked [HAS-IMAGE] come with a
usable photograph - prefer those for the large picture tiles.

LAYOUT MODEL
The body is a list of rows. You do not write rows: you write tiles in order, each with a width
"w" of 1, 2 or 3, and they are packed into rows of total width 3. So [w:2, w:1] is one row,
[w:1, w:1, w:1] is another, [w:3] is a full-width row. ALWAYS make each row's widths sum to 3.

TILE TYPES
  story    w:1 or 2  THE WORKHORSE. A news item, IMAGE-FIRST. "ref" = the [n] number of its
                     article; that article's own photo becomes the tile's picture, so ALWAYS
                     prefer articles marked [HAS-IMAGE]. Fields: tag, title (max 8 words),
                     source, date, why_it_matters (ONE sentence, max 20 words). No bullets.
  visual   w:2 or 3  A big picture tile built from an article's photo. Needs "ref" pointing at
                     a [HAS-IMAGE] article, plus a "caption" (max 12 words). Use for the two or
                     three most striking images of the week.
  stat     w:1       value (short, e.g. "71%", "$2B", "1,079") + label (max 8 words).
  quote    w:1 or 2  text (the sharpest line of the week) + attribution.
  chart    w:1 or 2  kicker, title, caption, spec {type: pie|bar|line|doughnut, labels[], values[]}.
                     Only numbers that actually appear in the articles.
  matrix   w:2 or 3  a 2x2 quadrant. title, x_labels[2], y_labels[2], cells[4] each {title, detail}.
                     Cell order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.
  ranked   w:1 or 2  title, items[] each {label, value (number), display}. 5-7 items.
  compare  w:2 or 3  title, row_header, columns[2-4], rows[] each {label, values[]}. A value is
                     a short string, or a number 0-3 (none/low/medium/high) shown as a shaded dot.
  flow     w:3       title, stages[] each {name, steps[] of 3-4 short labels}. A lifecycle.
  pipeline w:3       LEFT-TO-RIGHT ARCHITECTURE DIAGRAM, boxes joined by arrows. title,
                     nodes[3-5] each {name (max 3 words), detail (max 8 words)}. Use for any
                     "A feeds B feeds C" idea: data pipeline, RAG flow, agent loop, network path.
  timeline w:3       THE WEEK AS A LINE. title, events[4-6] each {date (e.g. "4 Aug"),
                     label (max 6 words)}. Use once per issue to show how the week unfolded.
  layers   w:2 or 3  MATURITY STAIRCASE, each step wider and darker. title, steps[3-5] each
                     {name, detail (max 10 words)}. Use for evolution, maturity levels,
                     capability tiers, adoption stages.
  tool     w:1       name + what (max 9 words).
  takeaway w:1       title (max 5 words) + detail (one action).

Return ONLY a JSON object, no markdown fence, no commentary:

{
  "title": "InfiniAI Pulse",
  "issue_no": "${issueNo}",
  "week_label": "${weekLabel}",
  "sections": [
    { "type": "cover",
      "intro": "<ONE sentence, max 28 words. This becomes the navy band printed at the top of EVERY page, so keep it tight>",
      "topics": ["<5-6 one-word themes>"],
      "hero_image_query": "<image search phrase for a strong banner graphic on this week's theme>",
      "hero_caption": "<max 12 words>" },

    { "type": "tiles", "heading": "This week at a glance",
      "summary": "<ONE sentence, max 28 words, describing THIS PAGE. Printed in the navy band at the top of page 2>",
      "items": [ <3 stat tiles w:1, then a mix of visual / story / quote tiles> ] },

    { "type": "tiles", "heading": "By the numbers",
      "summary": "<ONE sentence, max 28 words, describing THIS PAGE. Printed in the navy band at the top of page 3>",
      "items": [ <chart, ranked, matrix and compare tiles - the analytical page> ] },

    { "type": "tiles", "heading": "How it fits together",
      "summary": "<ONE sentence, max 28 words, describing THIS PAGE. Printed in the navy band at the top of page 4>",
      "items": [ <a flow tile w:3, then tool tiles w:1, then takeaway tiles w:1> ] },

    { "type": "sources", "heading": "Sources",
      "items": [ { "title": "<short>", "url": "<url>" } ] }
  ]
}

REQUIREMENTS
- This is a PICTURE-LED publication, and the pictures come from the articles themselves.
  STRONGLY prefer articles marked [HAS-IMAGE] - a story you can illustrate is worth more
  than one you cannot. Only pick an unillustrated article if the news genuinely demands it.
- STRUCTURE. Write FOUR sections: one "cover", then THREE "tiles" sections, then
  a "sources" section. Each tiles section needs its own one-sentence "summary" -
  it is printed in the navy band at the top of a page.

- QUANTITY. Supply 26-34 tiles in total across the three tiles sections, in
  priority order - most important first. The layout engine decides where the page
  breaks fall and will drop anything that does not fit, so put your best material
  first and do not worry about page boundaries. Never supply fewer than 24 tiles:
  too few leaves the last page short.

- DIAGRAMS ARE THE POINT. Include FOUR OR FIVE of these, never two of the same kind
  side by side: pipeline, timeline, layers, matrix, ranked, compare, chart, flow.
  Spread them through the issue so no page is only photographs and no page is only boxes.
- Build every diagram from what the articles actually say. Do not invent figures. If a story
  describes an architecture, draw it as a "pipeline". If it describes stages of maturity,
  draw "layers". If it compares approaches, draw "compare". If it ranks things, draw "ranked".
- Exactly one "timeline" per issue, placed early, showing how the week unfolded.
- 3 tool tiles and 3 takeaway tiles (one row each).
- Every row must sum to w:3. Count as you go.
- EVERY "tiles" section needs its own "summary": one sentence, max 28 words, printed
  in the navy band at the top of that page. Each band must describe ITS OWN page -
  never repeat the cover intro or another page's band. A reader who reads only the
  four bands should understand the whole issue.
- Telco relevance is the tie-breaker on every editorial decision.

ARTICLES:
${feedText}`;

return [{ json: { prompt, issueNo, weekLabel, articleCount: a.length } }];
